questions.text: नव्या, कार्तिक तथा समीर एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 4:3:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । समीर को यह गारंटी दी गयी थी कि किसी भी वर्ष लाभ में उसका भाग ₹ 57,000 से कम नहीं होगा। इस कारण खाते में हुई किसी भी कमी को नव्या तथा कार्तिक बराबर-बराबर वहन करेंगे। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹ 4,00,000 था। कार्तिक द्वारा वहन की गयी कमी थी :
questions.text_english: Navya, Kartik and Samir were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3:1. Samir was given a guarantee that his share of profit in any year will not be less than ₹57,000. Any deficiency on this account was to be borne by Navya and Kartik equally. The firm earned a profit of ₹4,00,000 during the year ended 31st March, 2025. The amount of deficiency borne by Kartik was:
questions.solution: Samir's share of profit is calculated as ₹4,00,000 × (1/8) = ₹50,000. The guaranteed amount is ₹57,000, creating a total deficiency of ₹57,000 - ₹50,000 = ₹7,000. Since this deficiency is borne by Navya and Kartik equally, Kartik's share of the deficiency is ₹7,000 / 2 = ₹3,500.
questions.solution_hindi: समीर का लाभ में हिस्सा ₹4,00,000 × (1/8) = ₹50,000 है। गारंटीकृत राशि ₹57,000 है, जिससे कुल कमी ₹57,000 - ₹50,000 = ₹7,000 हो जाती है। चूँकि यह कमी नव्या और कार्तिक द्वारा बराबर-बराबर वहन की जानी है, इसलिए कार्तिक द्वारा वहन की गई कमी ₹7,000 / 2 = ₹3,500 होगी।

questions.text: नंदिता तथा प्रभा फर्नीचर का निर्माण करने वाली एक फर्म के साझेदार थे। वे 8:7 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में नंदिता ने ₹80,000 नगद तथा ₹ 20,000 के फर्नीचर का आहरण अपने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए किया। साझेदारी संलेख में साझेदारों के आहरण पर 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज लगाने का प्रावधान था। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए नंदिता के आहरण पर ब्याज की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Nandita and Prabha were partners in a firm manufacturing furniture. They were sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:7. During the year ended 31st March 2025, Nandita withdrew ₹80,000 in cash and ₹20,000 as furniture for her personal use. The partnership deed provided for charging interest on partner's drawings @ 6% p.a. The amount of interest on Nandita's drawings for the year ended 31st March 2025 was:
questions.solution: Total drawings by Nandita include both cash and furniture, which is ₹80,000 + ₹20,000 = ₹1,00,000. Since the exact dates of the drawings are not provided, interest is calculated for an average period of 6 months. Therefore, Interest on Drawings = ₹1,00,000 × (6/100) × (6/12) = ₹3,000.
questions.solution_hindi: नंदिता द्वारा किए गए कुल आहरण में नगद और फर्नीचर दोनों शामिल हैं, जो कि ₹80,000 + ₹20,000 = ₹1,00,000 है। चूँकि आहरण की सटीक तिथियाँ नहीं दी गई हैं, इसलिए ब्याज की गणना 6 महीने की औसत अवधि के लिए की जाती है। अतः आहरण पर ब्याज = ₹1,00,000 × (6/100) × (6/12) = ₹3,000 होगा।

options.A: कम्पनी के प्रारंभिक व्ययों को अपलिखित करने के लिए ।
options.B: कम्पनी के अंशों अथवा ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर दिए गए बट्टे की राशि अथवा व्ययों अथवा कमीशन का भुगतान अपलिखित करने के लिए ।

options_english.A: Writing off preliminary expenses of the company.
options_english.B: Writing off expenses of or commission paid or discount allowed on issue of shares or debentures of the company.
options_english.C: Issuing partly paid up bonus shares to the existing shareholders of the company.
options_english.D: Providing for premium payable on redemption of redeemable preference shares or debentures of the company.

sub_questions.solution: According to Section 52(2) of the Companies Act 2013, the Securities Premium Account can be utilized for issuing fully paid-up bonus shares, but it strictly cannot be used for issuing partly paid-up bonus shares to existing shareholders.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसी एक विकल्प का उत्तर दें:
questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text: दिलशाद, अजीत तथा दीपना एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । उनकी स्थायी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 5,00,000, ₹4,00,000 तथा ₹ 1,00,000 थी । 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के खाते बन्द करने के पश्चात् ज्ञात हुआ कि साझेदारों की पूँजी पर 7% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज लगाने के बदले 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज लगाया गया । उपरोक्त अशुद्धि को शुद्ध करने के लिए आवश्यक समायोजन प्रविष्टि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: Dilshad, Ajit and Deepna were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Their fixed capitals were: ₹5,00,000, ₹4,00,000 and ₹1,00,000 respectively. After closing the accounts for the year ended 31st March 2025, it was discovered that interest on partners' capitals was provided @ 6% p.a. instead of 7% p.a. The adjustment entry to rectify the above error will be :

options.A: दीपना का चालू खाता नाम 1,000, दिलशाद का चालू खाता जमा 1,000
options.B: दिलशाद का चालू खाता नाम 1,000, दीपना का चालू खाता जमा 1,000
options.C: दीपना का पूँजी खाता नाम 1,000, दिलशाद का पूँजी खाता जमा 1,000
options.D: दिलशाद का पूँजी खाता नाम 1,000, दीपना का पूँजी खाता जमा 1,000

options_english.A: Deepna's Current A/c Dr. 1,000 To Dilshad's Current A/c 1,000
options_english.B: Dilshad's Current A/c Dr. 1,000 To Deepna's Current A/c 1,000
options_english.C: Deepna's Capital A/c Dr. 1,000 To Dilshad's Capital A/c 1,000
options_english.D: Dilshad's Capital A/c Dr. 1,000 To Deepna's Capital A/c 1,000

sub_questions.solution: Interest was provided at 6% instead of 7%, resulting in a short-credit of 1% on fixed capitals. The short-credit amounts are: Dilshad = ₹5,000 (Cr), Ajit = ₹4,000 (Cr), Deepna = ₹1,000 (Cr), totaling ₹10,000. This ₹10,000 must be recovered by debiting the partners in their profit-sharing ratio (2:2:1), resulting in debits of ₹4,000 to Dilshad, ₹4,000 to Ajit, and ₹2,000 to Deepna. The net effect is a ₹1,000 credit to Dilshad (₹5,000 Cr - ₹4,000 Dr), nil for Ajit, and a ₹1,000 debit to Deepna (₹1,000 Cr - ₹2,000 Dr). Since capitals are fixed, the entry is routed through Current Accounts: Deepna's Current A/c Dr. 1,000 To Dilshad's Current A/c 1,000.

sub_questions.text: कबीर, दिव्या तथा मांशा एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5: 4 : 1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2025 से उन्होंने भविष्य के लाभ-हानि 4:1:5 के अनुपात में बाँटने का निर्णय लिया । इस उद्देश्य के लिए फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 3,00,000 किया गया। लाभ अनुपात में बदलाव के कारण ख्याति के लेखांकन के लिए आवश्यक रोजनामचा प्रविष्टि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: Kabir, Divya and Mansha were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:4:1. With effect from 1st April 2025, they decided to share the future profits and losses in the ratio of 4:1:5. For this purpose, the goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹3,00,000. The necessary journal entry for the treatment of goodwill because of change in profit sharing ratio will be:

options_english.A: Kabir's Capital A/c Dr. 75,000, Divya's Capital A/c Dr. 2,25,000 To Mansha's Capital A/c 3,00,000
options_english.B: Mansha's Capital A/c Dr. 3,00,000 To Kabir's Capital A/c 75,000, To Divya's Capital A/c 2,25,000
options_english.C: Mansha's Capital A/c Dr. 1,20,000 To Kabir's Capital A/c 30,000, To Divya's Capital A/c 90,000
options_english.D: Kabir's Capital A/c Dr. 30,000, Divya's Capital A/c Dr. 90,000 To Mansha's Capital A/c 1,20,000

sub_questions.solution: First, calculate the sacrifice or gain for each partner. Kabir's sacrifice = (5/10) - (4/10) = 1/10. Divya's sacrifice = (4/10) - (1/10) = 3/10. Mansha's gain = (5/10) - (1/10) = 4/10. Since Mansha gains, her Capital Account is debited by (4/10 × ₹3,00,000) = ₹1,20,000. The sacrificing partners are credited: Kabir by (1/10 × ₹3,00,000) = ₹30,000 and Divya by (3/10 × ₹3,00,000) = ₹90,000.

questions.text: एक साझेदारी फर्म के विघटन पर पूँजी की कमी सहित हानि का सर्वप्रथम भुगतान किया जायेगा :
questions.text_english: In case of dissolution of a partnership firm, the losses, including deficiencies of capital, shall be paid first:

options.A: साझेदारों द्वारा व्यक्तिगत रूप से तथा बराबर-बराबर
options.B: साझेदारों द्वारा व्यक्तिगत रूप से उनके लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात में

options_english.B: by partners individually in their profit sharing ratio
options_english.C: out of capital of the partners

questions.solution: Under the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (Section 48), in settling the accounts of a firm after dissolution, losses including deficiencies of capital must be paid first out of profits, then out of capital, and lastly, if necessary, by the partners individually in their profit-sharing ratio.
questions.solution_hindi: भारतीय साझेदारी अधिनियम, 1932 (धारा 48) के प्रावधानों के अनुसार, फर्म के विघटन पर खातों का निपटान करते समय, पूँजी की कमी सहित हानियों का भुगतान सर्वप्रथम लाभों में से किया जाएगा, फिर पूँजी में से और अंत में यदि आवश्यक हो तो व्यक्तिगत रूप से साझेदारों द्वारा उनके लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात में किया जाएगा।

sub_questions.text_english: Hira Ltd. invited applications for issuing 2,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of 10%. The whole amount was payable with application. Applications were received for 4,00,000 equity shares. The company decided to allot the shares on pro-rata basis to all the applicants. The amount refunded by the company was:
sub_questions.solution: The issue price per share is ₹10 + 10% premium = ₹11. The company received applications for 4,00,000 shares, resulting in total application money of ₹44,00,000. However, the company can only retain money for the 2,00,000 shares issued, which amounts to ₹22,00,000. Since the entire amount is payable on application, there are no future calls to adjust the excess money against. Therefore, despite a pro-rata allotment, the entire excess amount of ₹22,00,000 must be fully refunded.

questions.text: एक्सियोम लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 30,000, 12% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन एक निश्चित बट्टे की दर पर किया, जो तीन वर्ष पश्चात् 10% प्रीमियम पर शोधनीय थे। इन ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन से पूर्व प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते में ₹5,00,000 का शेष था तथा ऋणपत्र निर्गमन पर हुई हानि को अपलिखित करने के पश्चात् प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते का शेष ₹ 50,000 था। इन ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन किया गया :
questions.text_english: Xiom Ltd. issued 30,000, 12% debentures of ₹100 each at a certain rate of discount, redeemable at 10% premium after three years. Balance in Securities Premium Account before issuing these debentures was ₹5,00,000 and after writing off loss on issue of debentures, the balance in Securities Premium Account was ₹50,000. These debentures were issued at a discount of:
questions.solution: The total loss written off against the Securities Premium Account is ₹5,00,000 - ₹50,000 = ₹4,50,000. The total loss on the issue comprises the discount on issue and the premium payable on redemption. The premium on redemption is 10% of the face value (30,000 × ₹100), which equates to ₹3,00,000. Therefore, the discount on issue must be ₹4,50,000 - ₹3,00,000 = ₹1,50,000. The discount per debenture is ₹1,50,000 / 30,000 = ₹5. As a percentage of the ₹100 face value, the discount rate is 5%.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रतिभूति प्रीमियम खाते से अपलिखित कुल हानि ₹5,00,000 - ₹50,000 = ₹4,50,000 है। निर्गमन पर कुल हानि में निर्गमन पर बट्टा और शोधन पर देय प्रीमियम दोनों शामिल होते हैं। शोधन पर प्रीमियम अंकित मूल्य (30,000 × ₹100) का 10% है, जो ₹3,00,000 है। अतः निर्गमन पर बट्टा ₹4,50,000 - ₹3,00,000 = ₹1,50,000 होगा। प्रति ऋणपत्र बट्टा ₹1,50,000 / 30,000 = ₹5 है। ₹100 के अंकित मूल्य पर यह बट्टा दर 5% है।

sub_questions.text: जुबिन, निधि तथा रीना एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:1:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । फर्म प्रतिवर्ष 31 मार्च को अपनी पुस्तकें बंद करती है। 31 जुलाई, 2025 को रीना की मृत्यु हो गयी। पिछले स्थिति विवरण की तिथि से उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभ में उसके भाग की गणना पिछले वर्ष के लाभ के आधार पर की जानी थी। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में फर्म का लाभ ₹ 6,00,000 था। मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में रीना का भाग था
sub_questions.text_english: Zubin, Nidhi and Reena were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1:2. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. On 31st July, 2025 Reena died. Her share in the profits of the firm from the last balance sheet till the date of death was to be calculated on the basis of previous year's profit. The profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2025 was ₹6,00,000. Reena's share of profit till the date of her death was:
sub_questions.solution: Reena survived for 4 months in the current financial year (April, May, June, and July). Her share of the profit till her death is calculated based on the previous year's profit, proportionate to the time survived and her profit-sharing ratio. The calculation is: ₹6,00,000 × (4/12) × (2/5) = ₹80,000.

sub_questions.text: पुनीत तथा बिनी की फर्म के विघटन पर ₹ 56,000 की एक अलिखित परिसम्पत्ति ₹ 70,000 के एक अलिखित लेनदार को उसके दावे के पूर्ण निपटान में ₹ 50,000 में दे दी गयी तथा शेष का भुगतान उसे नगद किया गया। वसूली खाते को _______ से _______ किया जायेगा ।
sub_questions.text_english: On the dissolution of the partnership firm of Puneet and Binny, an unrecorded asset of ₹56,000 was given to an unrecorded creditor of ₹70,000 in settlement of his claim of ₹50,000 and the balance was paid to him in cash. Realisation Account will be _______ by _______
sub_questions.solution: When an unrecorded asset is given to a creditor to settle part of their claim, no journal entry is passed for that specific exchange. However, the balance of the creditor's claim must be paid in cash. The total claim is ₹70,000, and ₹50,000 of it is settled by the asset. The remaining balance of ₹20,000 is paid in cash. This cash payment requires an entry where the Realisation Account is debited by ₹20,000.

questions.text_english: Shiv, Riya and Rohit were partners in a firm. On 1st October, 2024 Rohit had given a loan of ₹2,00,000 to the firm, at an interest rate of 10% p.a. as per the partnership agreement. The accountant of the firm is emphasizing that interest on loan will be paid at 6% p.a. The amount of interest on loan paid to Rohit for the year ended 31st March, 2025 will be :
questions.solution: The partnership agreement explicitly specifies an interest rate of 10% p.a., which overrides the default rule of 6% p.a. applicable only in the absence of an agreement. The loan was provided on 1st October 2024, meaning interest is calculated for 6 months up to 31st March 2025. The interest amount is ₹2,00,000 × (10/100) × (6/12) = ₹10,000.
questions.solution_hindi: साझेदारी समझौते में स्पष्ट रूप से 10% प्रतिवर्ष ब्याज दर निर्दिष्ट है, जो 6% प्रतिवर्ष के डिफ़ॉल्ट नियम (जो केवल समझौते के अभाव में लागू होता है) को निरस्त करती है। ऋण 1 अक्टूबर 2024 को दिया गया था, इसलिए 31 मार्च 2025 तक 6 महीने के लिए ब्याज की गणना की जाएगी। ब्याज की राशि = ₹2,00,000 × (10/100) × (6/12) = ₹10,000 होगी।

On the date of Rajat's retirement, the Balance Sheet of the firm showed a balance of ₹2,40,000 in Workmen Compensation Fund. The claim on account of workmen compensation amounted to ₹1,80,000. The amount credited to Rajat's capital account on the treatment of Workmen Compensation Fund would be
sub_questions.solution: The Workmen Compensation Fund has a balance of ₹2,40,000. Out of this, ₹1,80,000 is required to meet the claim, leaving an excess of ₹60,000. This excess amount is distributed among all partners in their old profit-sharing ratio (2:3:1). Rajat's share is 3/6 of the excess, which evaluates to ₹60,000 × (3/6) = ₹30,000.

Meera retired and Varun and Tarun decided to share future profits and losses equally. On Meera's retirement, the goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹5,00,000. The amount that was debited to Varun's and Tarun's capital account for the treatment of goodwill was:
sub_questions.solution: First, find the gaining ratio. Old ratio is 5:2:3. New ratio for Varun and Tarun is 1:1. Varun's gain = (1/2) - (2/10) = 3/10. Tarun's gain = (1/2) - (3/10) = 2/10. The gaining ratio is 3:2. Meera's share of goodwill is ₹5,00,000 × (5/10) = ₹2,50,000. This amount is contributed by Varun and Tarun in their gaining ratio. Varun's debit = ₹2,50,000 × (3/5) = ₹1,50,000. Tarun's debit = ₹2,50,000 × (2/5) = ₹1,00,000.

questions.solution: The profit-sharing ratio is 4:3:2. Tarush's share is 2/9 of the total profit, which is given as ₹1,80,000. The total profit of the firm is therefore ₹1,80,000 × (9/2) = ₹8,10,000. Amita's share is 4/9 of the total profit, which equals ₹8,10,000 × (4/9) = ₹3,60,000.

questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को वीनार लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के ₹ 5,00,000, 9% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% बट्टे पर किया । ब्याज अर्धवार्षिक आधार पर प्रतिवर्ष 30 सितम्बर तथा 31 मार्च को देय होता है। 31 मार्च, 2025 को अपलिखित ब्याज की राशि थी :

questions.solution: Interest on debentures is always calculated on the nominal face value. The total face value is ₹5,00,000. For a full year, the interest at 9% is ₹5,00,000 × 9% = ₹45,000. The phrase 'interest written off on 31st March, 2025' refers to the total interest expense transferred to the Statement of Profit and Loss for the year, which is the full ₹45,000.

questions.text_english: Bishan Ltd. acquired assets worth ₹12,60,000 and took over liabilities of ₹2,40,000 of Nimi Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹9,40,000. Bishan Ltd. issued 12% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 6% in favour of Nimi Ltd. for payment of purchase consideration. The number of debentures issued were:
questions.solution: The agreed purchase consideration is ₹9,40,000. To settle this amount, debentures are issued at a 6% discount, making the issue price per debenture ₹100 - ₹6 = ₹94. The number of debentures issued is calculated by dividing the purchase consideration by the issue price: ₹9,40,000 / ₹94 = 10,000 debentures.
questions.solution_hindi: सहमति प्राप्त क्रय प्रतिफल ₹9,40,000 है। इस राशि का भुगतान करने के लिए 6% बट्टे पर ऋणपत्र जारी किए गए हैं, जिससे प्रति ऋणपत्र निर्गमन मूल्य ₹100 - ₹6 = ₹94 हो जाता है। जारी किए गए ऋणपत्रों की संख्या की गणना क्रय प्रतिफल को निर्गमन मूल्य से विभाजित करके की जाती है: ₹9,40,000 / ₹94 = 10,000 ऋणपत्र।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : सेवानिवृत्ति पर सेवानिवृत्त साझेदार अथवा मृत्यु पर मृतक साझेदार के निष्पादक ख्याति में उनके भाग के अधिकारी होते हैं।
कारण (R) : फर्म द्वारा ख्याति सभी विद्यमान साझेदारों (सेवानिवृत्त तथा मृतक साझेदारों सहित) के प्रयास से अर्जित की जाती है।
निम्न में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): The retiring partner or the executors of the deceased partner are entitled to their share of goodwill at the time of retirement or death.
Reason (R) : Goodwill is earned by the firm with the efforts of all the existing partners (including the retiring or deceased partner).
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही वर्णन है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) का सही वर्णन नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The assertion is factually correct, as retiring or deceased partners have a right to their share of the firm's goodwill. The reason is also correct and provides the exact logical basis for the assertion: goodwill is the result of the past joint efforts of all partners, so anyone leaving the firm must be compensated for their historical contribution to building that reputation.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन तथ्यात्मक रूप से सही है, क्योंकि सेवानिवृत्त होने वाले या मृतक साझेदारों को फर्म की ख्याति में अपने हिस्से का अधिकार होता है। कारण भी सही है और अभिकथन के लिए सटीक तार्किक आधार प्रदान करता है: ख्याति सभी साझेदारों के पिछले संयुक्त प्रयासों का परिणाम है, इसलिए फर्म छोड़ने वाले किसी भी व्यक्ति को उस प्रतिष्ठा को बनाने में उनके ऐतिहासिक योगदान के लिए मुआवजा दिया जाना चाहिए।

questions.text: वाणी, वान्या तथा अजय एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । वाणी सेवानिवृत्त हो गयी तथा उसके भाग को वान्या तथा अजय ने 2:3 के अनुपात में ले लिया। वाणी के सेवानिवृत्त होने के पश्चात् वान्या तथा अजय का नया लाभ अनुपात था :
questions.text_english: Vani, Vanya and Ajay were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. Vani retired and her share was taken over by Vanya and Ajay in the ratio of 2:3. The new profit sharing ratio between Vanya and Ajay after Vani's retirement was:
questions.solution: Vani's old share was 5/10. This share is acquired by Vanya and Ajay in a 2:3 ratio. Vanya's gain = (5/10) × (2/5) = 2/10. Ajay's gain = (5/10) × (3/5) = 3/10. Adding this to their existing shares: Vanya's new share = 3/10 + 2/10 = 5/10. Ajay's new share = 2/10 + 3/10 = 5/10. The new profit-sharing ratio is 5:5, which simplifies to 1:1.

questions.text: देवकी तथा नीना एक फर्म की साझेदार थीं तथा 4:3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थीं। फर्म के लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए अमर को एक नया साझेदार बनाया गया। अमर ने अपने भाग का 1/3 भाग देवकी से अधिग्रहण किया। अमर ने नीना से कितने भाग का अधिग्रहण किया ?
questions.text_english: Devki and Neena were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3. Amar was admitted as a new partner for 1/5th share in the profits of the firm. Amar acquired 1/3rd of his share from Devki. How much share did Amar acquire from Neena?
questions.solution: Amar's total share is 1/5. He acquires 1/3rd of his share from Devki. The remaining portion of his share must be acquired from Neena, which is 2/3rds of his total share. Therefore, the fraction acquired from Neena is (2/3) × (1/5) = 2/15.
questions.solution_hindi: अमर का कुल हिस्सा 1/5 है। वह अपने हिस्से का 1/3 भाग देवकी से प्राप्त करता है। उसके हिस्से का शेष भाग नीना से प्राप्त किया जाना चाहिए, जो कि उसके कुल हिस्से का 2/3 भाग है। इसलिए, नीना से प्राप्त किया गया भाग (2/3) × (1/5) = 2/15 है।

questions.text:
बोस तथा रॉय एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे। बोस ने अपने व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष में फर्म से निम्न राशियों का आहरण किया :
(i) प्रथम तीन महीनों में उसने प्रत्येक महीने के आरंभ में ₹3,000 का आहरण किया ।
(ii) शेष महीनों में उसने प्रत्येक महीने के अन्त में ₹ 4,000 का आहरण किया ।
आहरण पर 6% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज प्रभारित किया जाना था। फर्म की पुस्तकें प्रतिवर्ष 31 मार्च को बन्द होती हैं। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए बोस के आहरण पर ब्याज की गणना कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Bose and Roy were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:1. Bose withdrew the following amounts from the firm for personal use during the year ending 31st March, 2025:
(i) For the first three months, he withdrew ₹3,000 at the beginning of every month.
(ii) For the remaining months, he withdrew ₹4,000 at the end of every month.
Interest on drawings was to be charged @ 6% p.a. The books of the firm are closed on 31st March every year. Calculate interest on Bose's drawings for the year ending 31st March, 2025.

key_points: For the first three months (April, May, June): Withdrawals are ₹3,000 at the beginning of each month. Total Product = (3000×12) + (3000×11) + (3000×10) = 99,000. Interest = 99,000 × 6% × (1/12) = ₹495.
For the remaining nine months (July to March): Withdrawals are ₹4,000 at the end of each month. Total drawings = 4,000 × 9 = 36,000. Average period = (8 + 0) / 2 = 4 months.
Interest for the remaining months = 36,000 × 6% × (4/12) = ₹720.
Total Interest on Bose's drawings = ₹495 + ₹720 = ₹1,215.

questions.solution: The calculation of interest on drawings is split into two phases based on the withdrawal pattern. For the first three months (April, May, June), Bose withdrew ₹3,000 at the beginning of each month. The months remaining for these drawings are 12, 11, and 10 respectively. Using the product method, the total product is (3,000×12) + (3,000×11) + (3,000×10) = 99,000. The interest is 99,000 × 6/100 × 1/12, which gives ₹495. For the remaining nine months, he withdrew ₹4,000 at the end of each month. The total drawings for this period are ₹36,000. Since these are regular withdrawals at the end of the month over a 9-month span ending in March, the average period is calculated as (months left after first drawing + months left after last drawing) / 2 = (8 + 0) / 2 = 4 months. The interest for this segment is 36,000 × 6/100 × 4/12, which gives ₹720. Adding both amounts, the total interest on Bose's drawings is ₹495 + ₹720 = ₹1,215.

सरिता तथा वीना एक फर्म की साझेदार थी तथा 3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटती थी । 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को उनके पूँजी खातों तथा चालू खातों में निम्न शेष थे :
[Table showing Capital Accounts: Sarita 4,00,000, Veena 3,00,000. Current Accounts: Sarita 80,000 (Cr.), Veena 60,000 (Dr.)]
साझेदारी संलेख में प्रावधान था कि सरिता को ₹ 2,000 प्रतिमाह की दर से वेतन का भुगतान किया जायेगा जबकि वीना को वर्ष भर के लिए ₹ 30,000 का कमीशन मिलना था। पूँजी पर 8% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज देय होगा। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए सरिता तथा वीना के आहरण क्रमशः ₹ 20,000 तथा ₹ 15,000 थे। 31 मार्च, 2025 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए लाभ-हानि विनियोग खाता तैयार करने के पश्चात् सरिता तथा वीना के चालू खातों में फर्म के विभाज्य लाभ में उनके भाग के रूप में उनके चालू खातों में क्रमश ₹ 36,000 तथा ₹ 24,000 क्रेडिट किए गये।
सरिता तथा वीना के चालू खाते तैयार कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Sarita and Veena were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. The balance in their capital and current accounts as on 1st April, 2024 were as under:
The partnership deed provided that Sarita was to be paid salary @ ₹2,000 per month whereas Veena was to get commission of ₹30,000 for the year. Interest on capital was to be allowed @ 8% p.a. The drawings of Sarita and Veena for the year ended 31st March, 2025 were ₹20,000 and ₹15,000 respectively. After preparing Profit and Loss Appropriation Account for the year ended 31st March, 2025, ₹36,000 and ₹24,000 were credited respectively to the current accounts of Sarita and Veena as their share of divisible profit.
Prepare Current Accounts of Sarita and Veena.

key_points: Current Account Opening Balances: Sarita ₹80,000 on the credit side. Veena ₹60,000 on the debit side.
Credit side additions: Sarita's salary is ₹2,000 × 12 = ₹24,000. Veena's commission is ₹30,000.
Interest on fixed capital @ 8%: Sarita gets ₹32,000 (8% of 4L). Veena gets ₹24,000 (8% of 3L).
Share of divisible profits credited: Sarita ₹36,000. Veena ₹24,000.
Debit side deductions: Drawings for Sarita ₹20,000. Drawings for Veena ₹15,000.

Closing Balances: Sarita's total credit (80k+24k+32k+36k) = ₹1,72,000. Less 20k debit = ₹1,52,000 (Cr. balance). Veena's total credit (30k+24k+24k) = ₹78,000. Total debit (60k+15k) = ₹75,000. Balance = ₹3,000 (Cr. balance).

sub_questions.solution: To prepare the Current Accounts of Sarita and Veena, begin with their opening balances: Sarita has a credit balance of ₹80,000, and Veena has a debit balance of ₹60,000. On the credit side, post all appropriations. Sarita is credited with her annual salary of ₹24,000 (₹2,000 × 12), and Veena is credited with her commission of ₹30,000. Interest on their fixed capitals at 8% per annum yields a credit of ₹32,000 for Sarita and ₹24,000 for Veena. Finally, credit their given shares of divisible profit: ₹36,000 for Sarita and ₹24,000 for Veena. On the debit side, record their drawings: ₹20,000 for Sarita and ₹15,000 for Veena. Balancing the accounts gives Sarita a total credit of ₹1,72,000 and a debit of ₹20,000, resulting in a closing credit balance of ₹1,52,000. For Veena, the total credit is ₹78,000 and the total debit is ₹75,000, leaving a closing credit balance of ₹3,000.

sub_questions.text:
मान्या, विवेक तथा विशाल एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2025 से उन्होंने भविष्य में लाभ एवं हानि को 3:5:2 के अनुपात में बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। 31 मार्च, 2025 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्न शेष दर्शा रहा था :
(i) सामान्य संचय ₹ 2,40,000
(ii) लाभ-हानि खाते में ₹ 60,000 का डेबिट शेष
फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 6,00,000 किया गया तथा परिसम्पत्तियों के पुनर्मूल्यांकन व देयताओं के पुनर्निर्धारण पर ₹ 2,00,000 का लाभ हुआ। साझेदारों ने सामान्य संचय तथा लाभ-हानि खाते की राशि को बाँटने का निर्णय लिया। उन्होंने यह भी निर्णय लिया कि परिसम्पत्तियों तथा देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकन मूल्यों का लेखा, पुस्तकों में नहीं किया जायेगा।
उपरोक्त को प्रभावी करने के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Manya, Vivek and Vishal were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. With effect from 1st April, 2025, they decided to share future profits and losses in the ratio of 3:5:2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2025 showed the following balances:
(i) General Reserve ₹2,40,000.
(ii) Debit balance of ₹60,000 in Profit and Loss Account.
Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹6,00,000 and revaluation of assets and re-assessment of liabilities resulted in a gain of ₹2,00,000. Partners decided to distribute the amount of General Reserve and Profit and Loss Account. They also decided that revalued values of assets and liabilities were not to be recorded in the books.
Pass necessary journal entries to give effect to the above.

key_points: Entry 1 (Distribution of Reserve): General Reserve A/c Dr. ₹2,40,000 To Manya's Cap A/c ₹1,20,000, To Vivek's Cap A/c ₹72,000, To Vishal's Cap A/c ₹48,000 (in 5:3:2).
Entry 2 (Distribution of P&L Dr. Balance): Manya's Cap A/c Dr. ₹30,000, Vivek's Cap A/c Dr. ₹18,000, Vishal's Cap A/c Dr. ₹12,000 To P&L A/c ₹60,000 (in 5:3:2).
Calculate net effect for Goodwill and Revaluation: Goodwill (₹6,00,000) + Revaluation Gain (₹2,00,000) = ₹8,00,000 to be adjusted via capital accounts.
Calculate Sacrifice/Gain: Manya = 5/10 - 3/10 = 2/10 (Sacrifice). Vivek = 3/10 - 5/10 = -2/10 (Gain). Vishal = 2/10 - 2/10 = Nil.
Entry 3 (Adjustment Entry): Vivek's Cap A/c Dr. ₹1,60,000 (8,00,000 × 2/10) To Manya's Cap A/c ₹1,60,000.

sub_questions.solution: There are three distinct journal entries required to implement the partners' decisions. First, since they chose to distribute accumulated reserves, the General Reserve of ₹2,40,000 must be fully divided in the old ratio of 5:3:2. This debits the General Reserve Account and credits Manya with ₹1,20,000, Vivek with ₹72,000, and Vishal with ₹48,000. Second, the debit balance of the Profit and Loss Account (₹60,000) is written off similarly, debiting Manya with ₹30,000, Vivek with ₹18,000, and Vishal with ₹12,000, while crediting the Profit and Loss Account. Lastly, because the partners opted not to record the revised values of assets and liabilities, the Revaluation Gain of ₹2,00,000 is combined with the firm's Goodwill of ₹6,00,000, yielding an aggregate adjustment sum of ₹8,00,000. Analyzing the ratio change reveals that Manya sacrifices 2/10ths of her share, while Vivek gains 2/10ths (Vishal has no change). Therefore, an adjustment entry is passed, debiting Vivek's Capital Account and crediting Manya's Capital Account with 2/10ths of ₹8,00,000, which evaluates precisely to ₹1,60,000.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text:
मिराया लिमिटेड ने विशाल लिमिटेड की ₹ 70,00,000 की परिसम्पत्तियों तथा ₹ 12,00,000 की देयताओं को ₹ 64,00,000 के क्रय प्रतिफल के बदले ले लिया। विशाल लिमिटेड को क्रय प्रतिफल का भुगतान ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 50,000, 11% ऋणपत्रों को 20% प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करके तथा शेष का भुगतान चैक द्वारा किया गया ।
मिराया लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेनदेनों की आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Miraya Ltd. took over assets of ₹70,00,000 and liabilities of ₹12,00,000 of Vishal Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹64,00,000. The payment of purchase consideration was made by issue of 50,000, 11% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of 20% to Vishal Ltd. and the balance through a cheque.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Miraya Ltd.

key_points: Calculate Goodwill: Net Assets acquired = ₹70,00,000 - ₹12,00,000 = ₹58,00,000. Since PC (₹64,00,000) > Net Assets, Goodwill is ₹6,00,000.
Entry 1: Sundry Assets A/c Dr. ₹70,00,000, Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹6,00,000 To Sundry Liabilities ₹12,00,000, To Vishal Ltd. ₹64,00,000.
Calculate Debenture Issue: 50,000 debentures at ₹120 (₹100 face value + 20% premium). Total value = ₹60,00,000. Therefore, Bank payment = ₹64,00,000 - ₹60,00,000 = ₹4,00,000.
Entry 2: Vishal Ltd. Dr. ₹64,00,000 To 11% Debentures A/c ₹50,00,000, To Securities Premium A/c ₹10,00,000, To Bank A/c ₹4,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: The first step is to record the acquisition. The net assets taken over are valued at ₹58,00,000 (Assets of ₹70,00,000 minus Liabilities of ₹12,00,000). The agreed purchase consideration is ₹64,00,000, which exceeds the net assets by ₹6,00,000. This excess amount is recorded as Goodwill. The first journal entry debits Sundry Assets for ₹70,00,000 and Goodwill for ₹6,00,000, while crediting Sundry Liabilities for ₹12,00,000 and Vishal Ltd. for ₹64,00,000. Next, we record the settlement of the purchase consideration. Miraya Ltd. issues 50,000 debentures with a face value of ₹100 at a 20% premium, making the issue price ₹120 per debenture. This fulfills ₹60,00,000 of the obligation (debited to Vishal Ltd., with ₹50,00,000 credited to 11% Debentures and ₹10,00,000 credited to Securities Premium). The remaining balance of ₹4,00,000 is settled by cheque, thereby crediting the Bank Account.

sub_questions.text:
डेल्टा लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 30,000, 9% ऋणपत्रों को ₹30 प्रति ऋणपत्र के प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए। सम्पूर्ण राशि का भुगतान आवेदन पर देय था। 40,000 ऋणपत्रों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए। 2,000 ऋणपत्रों के आवेदनों को अस्वीकार कर दिया गया तथा आवेदन राशि वापिस कर दी गई। शेष आवेदकों को आनुपातिक आधार पर ऋणपत्रों का आबंटन कर दिया गया ।
डेल्टा लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेनदेनों की आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english:
Delta Ltd. invited applications for issuing 30,000, 9% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of ₹30 per debenture. The full amount was payable on application. Applications were received for 40,000 debentures. Applications for 2,000 debentures were rejected and the application money was refunded. Debentures were allotted to the remaining applicants on pro rata basis.
Pass the necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Delta Ltd.

key_points: Issue price is ₹130 (₹100 face value + ₹30 premium).
Total application money received = 40,000 × ₹130 = ₹52,00,000.
Entry 1: Bank A/c Dr. ₹52,00,000 To Debenture Application & Allotment A/c ₹52,00,000.
Allotment of 30,000 debentures utilizes ₹39,00,000 (Capital ₹30,00,000 + Premium ₹9,00,000).
The remaining 10,000 applications cannot be adjusted as no future calls exist (full amount paid on application). Thus, all excess money (10,000 × ₹130 = ₹13,00,000) must be refunded.
Entry 2: Debenture Application & Allotment A/c Dr. ₹52,00,000 To 9% Debentures A/c ₹30,00,000, To Securities Premium A/c ₹9,00,000, To Bank A/c ₹13,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: Since the full amount is payable on application, the issue price per debenture is ₹130. The company initially receives application money for 40,000 debentures, generating a total receipt of ₹52,00,000. This is recorded by debiting the Bank Account and crediting the Debenture Application & Allotment Account for ₹52,00,000. During the allotment phase, the company can only allocate 30,000 debentures, requiring an allocation of ₹30,00,000 to the 9% Debentures Account and ₹9,00,000 to the Securities Premium Account. Although only 2,000 applications were explicitly rejected, the pro-rata allocation for the remainder means there is still excess application money. Because no future calls exist, all surplus funds encompassing the 10,000 over-applied debentures (10,000 × ₹130) must be entirely refunded. Thus, the second journal entry debits Debenture Application & Allotment for ₹52,00,000, while crediting 9% Debentures for ₹30,00,000, Securities Premium for ₹9,00,000, and the Bank Account for the total refund of ₹13,00,000.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text: पिछले कुछ वर्षों में एक फर्म का औसत लाभ ₹ 1,60,000 था। समान प्रकार के व्यवसाय में लाभ की सामान्य दर 10% है। यदि चार वर्षों के अधिलाभ के क्रय पर फर्म की ख्याति ₹ 4,00,000 है, तो फर्म द्वारा निवेशित पूँजी की गणना कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Average profits of a firm during the last few years were ₹1,60,000. The normal rate of return in a similar business is 10%. If the goodwill of the firm is ₹4,00,000 at four years purchase of super profit, find the capital employed by the firm.

key_points: Goodwill = Super Profit × Number of years purchase.
Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit.
Normal Profit = Capital Employed × Normal Rate of Return.

sub_questions.solution: Working backward from the goodwill valuation, we know that Goodwill (₹4,00,000) equals Super Profit multiplied by the number of years' purchase (4). This means the Super Profit must be ₹1,00,000. By definition, Super Profit is the excess of Average Profit over Normal Profit. Given the Average Profit is ₹1,60,000, subtracting the Super Profit of ₹1,00,000 determines the Normal Profit to be ₹60,000. Since Normal Profit represents the expected return (10%) on the Capital Employed, we calculate the Capital Employed by dividing the Normal Profit by the normal rate of return. Thus, ₹60,000 divided by 10% yields a Capital Employed of ₹6,00,000.

sub_questions.text:
एक व्यवसाय ने पिछले तीन वर्षों में ₹ 60,000 का औसत लाभ अर्जित किया। इसी प्रकार के व्यवसाय में प्रतिफल की सामान्य दर 12% है। व्यवसाय की निवल सम्पत्तियों का मूल्य ₹ 4,00,000 है। ख्याति के मूल्य की गणना कीजिए :
(i) औसत लाभों के पूँजीकरण विधि द्वारा
(ii) अधिलाभों के पूँजीकरण विधि द्वारा
sub_questions.text_english:
A business earned average profits of ₹60,000 during the last three years. The normal rate of return on similar business is 12%. The value of net assets of the business is ₹4,00,000. Calculate the value of goodwill by:
(i) Capitalisation of average profits method.
(ii) Capitalisation of super profits method.

key_points: (i) Capitalisation of Average Profits: Capitalized value of firm = Average Profit / NRR = ₹60,000 / 12% = ₹5,00,000. Goodwill = Capitalized Value - Net Assets = ₹5,00,000 - ₹4,00,000 = ₹1,00,000.

(ii) Capitalisation of Super Profits: Normal Profit = 12% of Net Assets (₹4,00,000) = ₹48,000. Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit = ₹60,000 - ₹48,000 = ₹12,000. Goodwill = Super Profit / NRR = ₹12,000 / 12% = ₹1,00,000.

sub_questions.solution: For the capitalisation of average profits method, we first determine the total capitalized value of the business by dividing the average profit of ₹60,000 by the normal rate of return (12%), which gives ₹5,00,000. Subtracting the actual net assets (₹4,00,000) from this capitalized value yields a goodwill of ₹1,00,000. Alternatively, for the capitalisation of super profits method, we calculate the normal profit expected on the net assets, which is 12% of ₹4,00,000, equaling ₹48,000. The super profit is the difference between the average profit and this normal profit, evaluating to ₹12,000. Capitalizing this super profit at 12% (₹12,000 divided by 12%) produces the exact same goodwill valuation of ₹1,00,000.

questions.text:
मिताली लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में निम्न लेनदेनों के लिए ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 7000, 9% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% बट्टे पर किया गया, जिनका शोधन 5 वर्षों पश्चात् 5% प्रीमियम पर किया जायेगा ।
(ii) ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 8000, 11% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 10% प्रीमियम पर किया गया जिनका शोधन 5 वर्षों पश्चात् 5% प्रीमियम पर किया जायेगा ।
questions.text_english:
Pass necessary journal entries in the books of Mitali Ltd. for issue of debentures in the following cases:
(i) Issued 7,000, 9% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 10%, redeemable at a premium of 5% after 5 years.
(ii) Issued 8,000, 11% debentures of ₹100 each at a premium of 10%, redeemable at a premium of 5% after 5 years.

key_points: Case (i): Debentures issued at a discount, redeemable at premium. Face value = ₹7,00,000. Discount = ₹70,000. Premium on Redemption = ₹35,000. Total Loss = ₹1,05,000. Amount received = ₹6,30,000.
Entry 1: Bank A/c Dr. ₹6,30,000 To Debenture Application and Allotment A/c ₹6,30,000.
Entry 2: Debenture Application and Allotment A/c Dr. ₹6,30,000, Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr. ₹1,05,000 To 9% Debentures A/c ₹7,00,000, To Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c ₹35,000.

Case (ii): Debentures issued at a premium, redeemable at premium. Face value = ₹8,00,000. Securities Premium = ₹80,000. Premium on Redemption = ₹40,000. Loss on Issue = ₹40,000. Amount received = ₹8,80,000.
Entry 3: Bank A/c Dr. ₹8,80,000 To Debenture Application and Allotment A/c ₹8,80,000.

Entry 4: Debenture Application and Allotment A/c Dr. ₹8,80,000, Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c Dr. ₹40,000 To 11% Debentures A/c ₹8,00,000, To Securities Premium A/c ₹80,000, To Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c ₹40,000.

questions.solution: For the first case, Mitali Ltd. receives ₹6,30,000 in cash since the 7,000 debentures are issued at a 10% discount on their ₹100 face value. This requires debiting Bank A/c and crediting Debenture Application & Allotment A/c with ₹6,30,000. Next, this receipt is converted to capital liability by debiting Debenture Application & Allotment with ₹6,30,000 and debiting Loss on Issue of Debentures with the combined amount of the discount (₹70,000) and the future redemption premium (₹35,000), making the total loss ₹1,05,000. This is balanced by crediting the 9% Debentures A/c with the face value of ₹7,00,000 and Premium on Redemption with ₹35,000. For the second case, the 8,000 debentures are issued at a 10% premium, bringing in ₹8,80,000. The first entry debits Bank and credits Debenture Application & Allotment with ₹8,80,000. The subsequent allocation entry debits Debenture Application & Allotment for ₹8,80,000 and records the future redemption liability by debiting Loss on Issue for the 5% premium on redemption (₹40,000). The corresponding credits go to 11% Debentures for the face value of ₹8,00,000, Securities Premium for the issue premium of ₹80,000, and Premium on Redemption for ₹40,000.

questions.text:
विभिन्न परिसम्पत्तियों (नगद को छोड़कर) तथा बाह्य देयताओं को वसूली खाते में हस्तांतरित करने के पश्चात् अर्जुन तथा कुनाल की फर्म के विघटन पर निम्न लेनदेनों के लिए आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) अर्जुन को विघटन कार्य की देखरेख करने के लिए नियुक्त किया गया था जिसके लिए उसे ₹ 10,000 का वेतन दिया जायेगा। उसने वसूली व्ययों को वहन करने की सहमति दी। अर्जुन द्वारा भुगतान किए गए वास्तविक विघटन व्यय ₹ 9,500 थे ।
(ii) एक लेनदार, जिसे फर्म को ₹ 9,000 देने थे, ₹ 3,000 का स्टॉक 10% बट्टे पर लेने को सहमत हुआ तथा उसे शेष का भुगतान नगद किया गया ।
(iii) कुनाल ने फर्म को ₹ 20,000 का ऋण दिया हुआ था। उसे उसके ऋण के पूर्ण निपटान हेतु ₹ 19,000 का भुगतान किया गया ।
(iv) फर्नीचर के एक भाग को जिसका लेखा पुस्तकों में नहीं किया गया था तथा जिसका संभावित मूल्य ₹ 30,000 था, अर्जुन ने ₹ 27,000 में ले लिया।
questions.text_english:
Pass the necessary journal entries for the following transactions on the dissolution of the partnership firm of Arjun and Kunal after various assets (other than cash) and external liabilities have been transferred to Realisation Account:
(i) Arjun was appointed to look after dissolution work for which he was allowed a remuneration of ₹10,000. He agreed to bear the dissolution expenses. Actual dissolution expenses paid by Arjun were ₹9,500.
(ii) A creditor to whom the firm owed ₹9,000, accepted stock of ₹3,000 at a discount of 10% and the balance was paid to him in cash.
(iii) Kunal had given a loan of ₹20,000 to the firm. He was paid ₹19,000 in full settlement of his loan.
(iv) A piece of furniture, which was not recorded in the books was taken over by Arjun at ₹27,000 whereas its expected value was ₹30,000.

key_points: (i) Realisation A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Arjun's Capital A/c ₹10,000. (The actual expenses of ₹9,500 are a personal matter between Arjun and the firm's cash only if paid by the firm, but since Arjun bore and paid it, no entry is needed for the actual expenses.)

(ii) The creditor's claim was ₹9,000. They took stock worth ₹3,000 at a 10% discount, i.e., ₹2,700. No entry for the asset takeover. The remaining balance to be paid in cash = ₹9,000 - ₹2,700 = ₹6,300. Entry: Realisation A/c Dr. ₹6,300 To Bank A/c ₹6,300.
(iii) Kunal's Loan A/c Dr. ₹20,000 To Bank A/c ₹19,000, To Realisation A/c ₹1,000 (transferring the ₹1,000 benefit to Realisation).
(iv) An unrecorded asset is taken over by a partner. Entry: Arjun's Capital A/c Dr. ₹27,000 To Realisation A/c ₹27,000.

questions.solution: For transaction (i), the firm owes Arjun ₹10,000 for handling the dissolution process. This is recorded by debiting the Realisation Account and crediting Arjun's Capital Account with ₹10,000. Since he personally bore and paid the actual expenses of ₹9,500, no further entry is required in the firm's books. For transaction (ii), when a creditor accepts a firm asset to settle a portion of their debt, no journal entry is made for that specific exchange. The stock was accepted at an agreed value of ₹2,700 (10% discount on ₹3,000), leaving a balance of ₹6,300 (₹9,000 - ₹2,700). This balance is settled in cash, requiring a debit to the Realisation Account and a credit to the Bank Account for ₹6,300. For transaction (iii), settling a partner's loan for less than its book value results in a gain. Debit Kunal's Loan Account for its full value of ₹20,000, credit Bank Account for the ₹19,000 paid, and credit the remaining ₹1,000 directly to the Realisation Account. For transaction (iv), when a partner takes over an unrecorded asset, it is treated as a realization. The entry debits Arjun's Capital Account and credits the Realisation Account for the mutually agreed value of ₹27,000, entirely ignoring the hypothetical expected value.

questions.text_english:
Shanta Ltd. has an authorized capital of ₹30,00,000 divided into equity shares of ₹100 each. The company invited applications for issuing 28,000 shares. Applications for 27,000 shares were received and allotment was made to all the applicants in full. All calls were made and were duly received except on 300 shares on which the final call of ₹20 per share was not received. The company forfeited 200 of these shares on which final call was not received.
Answer the following questions:

sub_questions.text: कम्पनी की प्राधिकृत पूँजी है :
sub_questions.text_english: The nominal capital of the company is :
sub_questions.solution: The nominal or authorized capital is the maximum amount of share capital a company is permitted to issue, which the passage explicitly states is ₹30,00,000.

sub_questions.text: कम्पनी की निर्गमित पूँजी है :
sub_questions.text_english: The issued capital of the company is :
sub_questions.solution: The issued capital represents the portion of authorized capital offered to the public for subscription. The company invited applications for 28,000 shares at ₹100 each, making the issued capital ₹28,00,000.

sub_questions.text: शांता लिमिटेड की अभिदत्त एवं पूर्ण प्रदत्त पूँजी है:
sub_questions.text_english: Subscribed and fully paid-up capital of Shanta Ltd. is:
sub_questions.solution: The company originally received applications for 27,000 shares. However, 300 shares fell into arrears. This leaves exactly 26,700 shares that are fully paid up. Multiplying these shares by the ₹100 face value yields a subscribed and fully paid-up capital of ₹26,70,000.

sub_questions.text: शांता लिमिटेड के स्थिति विवरण में दर्शायी जाने वाली 'अंश पूँजी' की राशि होगी:
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of 'share capital' presented in the balance sheet of Shanta Ltd. will be:
sub_questions.solution: The total share capital in the balance sheet comprises three parts: Subscribed & Fully Paid (26,700 shares × ₹100 = ₹26,70,000), Subscribed but Not Fully Paid (100 remaining unforfeited shares in arrears: ₹10,000 called up minus ₹2,000 unpaid = ₹8,000), and the Share Forfeiture Account balance (200 forfeited shares × ₹80 paid = ₹16,000). The total sum is ₹26,70,000 + ₹8,000 + ₹16,000 = ₹26,94,000.

sub_questions.text: 'खातों के नोट्स' में 'अंशहरण खाते' के अन्तर्गत दर्शायी गयी राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: In the 'Notes to Accounts', the amount disclosed under 'Share Forfeiture Account' will be:
sub_questions.solution: The Share Forfeiture Account reflects the actual capital amount collected on shares that were subsequently forfeited. Out of the 300 shares in default, 200 were forfeited. Since the final call was ₹20, these 200 shares had already paid ₹80 each. The forfeited amount is 200 × ₹80 = ₹16,000.

sub_questions.text: 'खातों के नोट्स' में दर्शायी जाने वाली 'अदत्त याचना राशि' होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of 'calls in arrears' disclosed in 'Notes to Accounts' will be:
sub_questions.solution: Initially, 300 shares were in arrears for the ₹20 final call, creating total arrears of ₹6,000. However, once 200 of those shares were forfeited, their associated arrears were cancelled. This leaves 100 active shares that still have unpaid calls. The remaining 'calls in arrears' balance is 100 shares × ₹20 = ₹2,000.

अनीश, बिन्दु तथा चाँदनी एक फर्म के साझेदार थे तथा 2:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि बाँटते थे । 31 दिसम्बर, 2023 को अनीश की मृत्यु हो गयी। सभी आवश्यक समायोजनों के पश्चात् अनीश का पूँजी खाता ₹ 5,00,000 का क्रेडिट शेष दर्शा रहा था । 1 जनवरी, 2024 को अनीश के निष्पादकों को ₹ 1,00,000 का नगद भुगतान कर दिया गया तथा शेष का भुगतान अदत्त राशि पर 12% वार्षिक दर के ब्याज सहित 31 दिसम्बर, 2024 से प्रारम्भ करके दो बराबर वार्षिक किश्तों में किया जाना था। फर्म अपनी पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद करती है।
राशि के पूर्ण भुगतान तक अनीश के निष्पादकों का खाता तैयार कीजिए ।
questions.text_english:
Anish, Bindu and Chandni were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:2:1. Anish died on 31st December, 2023. After all necessary adjustments, Anish's Capital Account showed a credit balance of ₹5,00,000. Anish's executors were paid ₹1,00,000 in cash on 1st January, 2024 and the balance in two equal yearly instalments starting from 31st December, 2024 with interest @ 12% p.a. on the unpaid amount. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year.
Prepare Anish's Executors Account till the amount is finally paid.

key_points: Transfer from Anish's Capital A/c on Dec 31, 2023: Credit Executors A/c with ₹5,00,000.
Payment on Jan 1, 2024: Debit Executors A/c with ₹1,00,000. Remaining principal balance is ₹4,00,000.
Interest from Jan 1, 2024 to March 31, 2024 (3 months): 12% on ₹4,00,000 = ₹12,000. Balance carried down on Mar 31, 2024 is ₹4,12,000.
Interest from April 1, 2024 to Dec 31, 2024 (9 months): 12% on ₹4,00,000 = ₹36,000. Total interest for the instalment year is ₹48,000.
First Instalment paid on Dec 31, 2024: Principal ₹2,00,000 + Interest ₹48,000 = ₹2,48,000.
Interest from Jan 1, 2025 to March 31, 2025 (3 months): 12% on remaining ₹2,00,000 = ₹6,000. Balance carried down on Mar 31, 2025 is ₹2,06,000.
Interest from April 1, 2025 to Dec 31, 2025 (9 months): 12% on ₹2,00,000 = ₹18,000. Total interest for the second instalment year is ₹24,000.
Final Instalment paid on Dec 31, 2025: Principal ₹2,00,000 + Interest ₹24,000 = ₹2,24,000. Account closed.

questions.solution: Begin Anish's Executors Account on December 31, 2023, by crediting the fully adjusted capital balance of ₹5,00,000. On January 1, 2024, record the immediate cash payment by debiting ₹1,00,000, leaving an outstanding principal of ₹4,00,000 to be paid in two equal yearly instalments of ₹2,00,000. Because the firm's financial year closes on March 31, interest must be accrued. Calculate 3 months of interest on ₹4,00,000 at 12% p.a., crediting ₹12,000 on March 31, 2024. Bring down the balance of ₹4,12,000 to April 1, 2024. Next, calculate 9 months of interest (April to December) on the ₹4,00,000 principal, yielding ₹36,000. On December 31, 2024, the first instalment is paid: ₹2,00,000 principal plus the combined ₹48,000 interest, totaling ₹2,48,000. Accrue interest again for the remaining 3 months until March 31, 2025, on the new ₹2,00,000 principal, giving ₹6,000. Bring down the ₹2,06,000 balance to April 1, 2025. Finally, calculate 9 months of interest on the ₹2,00,000 principal, adding ₹18,000. Pay the final instalment on December 31, 2025, comprising the ₹2,00,000 principal and the ₹24,000 total interest, effectively discharging the entire liability and closing the account.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following options:

sub_questions.text:
निम्न स्थितियों में अंशों के हरण तथा हरण किए गए अंशों के पुनः निर्गमन की आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए :
(i) सान्या लिमिटेड ने ₹ 2 प्रति अंश के प्रीमियम पर निर्गमित ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 2000 अंशों जिन पर ₹8 प्रति अंश माँगा गया था, ₹5 प्रति अंश की आबंटन राशि (प्रीमियम सहित) का भुगतान न करने पर हरण कर लिया। इन अंशों में से 700 अंशों को ₹ 10 प्रति अंश ₹8 प्रदत्त पर देव को पुनः निर्गमित कर दिया गया ।
(ii) मोक्ष लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 5000 अंशों को जिन पर ₹3 प्रति अंश की प्रथम याचना प्राप्त नहीं हुई थी, का हरण कर लिया। ₹ 2 प्रति अंश की दूसरी तथा अन्तिम याचना अभी तक माँगी नहीं गयी थी। इनमें से 2000 अंशों को ₹7 प्रति अंश, ₹8 प्रदत्त पर गीता को पुनः निर्गमित कर दिया गया ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Pass necessary journal entries for forfeiture and reissue of forfeited shares in the following cases:
(i) Sanya Ltd. forfeited 2,000 shares of ₹10 each, issued at a premium of ₹2 per share, ₹8 called up, for non-payment of allotment money of ₹5 per share (including premium). Out of these, 700 shares were reissued to Dev as ₹8 paid up for ₹10 per share.
(ii) Moksh Ltd. forfeited 5,000 shares of ₹10 each on which first call of ₹3 per share was not received. The second and final call of ₹2 per share has not yet been called. Out of these, 2,000 shares were issued to Geeta as ₹8 paid up for ₹7 per share.

key_points: Case (i) Forfeiture: Called up capital = ₹8. Unpaid allotment = ₹5 (Capital ₹3 + Premium ₹2). Since premium is not paid, debit Securities Premium. Amount paid on application = ₹8 called - ₹3 unpaid capital = ₹5. Entry: Share Capital Dr. ₹16,000, Securities Premium Dr. ₹4,000 To Share Allotment ₹10,000, To Share Forfeiture ₹10,000.
Case (i) Reissue: Reissued 700 shares at ₹10, as ₹8 paid up. This is a reissue at a premium. Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹7,000 To Share Capital ₹5,600, To Securities Premium ₹1,400.
Case (i) Capital Reserve: Transfer the entire forfeited amount corresponding to 700 shares. 700 × ₹5 = ₹3,500. Entry: Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. ₹3,500 To Capital Reserve ₹3,500.

Case (ii) Forfeiture: Called up capital = ₹8 (₹10 - ₹2 uncalled). Unpaid = ₹3. Paid = ₹5. Entry: Share Capital Dr. ₹40,000 To Calls in Arrears (or Share First Call) ₹15,000, To Share Forfeiture ₹25,000.
Case (ii) Reissue: 2,000 shares reissued at ₹7, as ₹8 paid up. Discount = ₹1 per share. Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹14,000, Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. ₹2,000 To Share Capital ₹16,000.
Case (ii) Capital Reserve: Forfeited amount for 2,000 shares = 2,000 × ₹5 = ₹10,000. Less discount utilized ₹2,000 = ₹8,000. Entry: Share Forfeiture A/c Dr. ₹8,000 To Capital Reserve ₹8,000.

sub_questions.solution: For Sanya Ltd., the capital called up is ₹8 per share. The allotment of ₹5 contains ₹2 premium, meaning ₹3 of capital was unpaid. Thus, ₹5 was already paid on application. Debit Share Capital for ₹16,000 (2,000×8) and Securities Premium for ₹4,000 (2,000×2), while crediting Share Allotment for ₹10,000 and Share Forfeiture for ₹10,000. On reissue of 700 shares at ₹10 (when only ₹8 is treated as paid), there is a ₹2 premium. Debit Bank with ₹7,000 and credit Share Capital with ₹5,600 and Securities Premium with ₹1,400. Since no discount was given, the full forfeited amount for these 700 shares (700×5 = ₹3,500) is transferred directly to Capital Reserve. For Moksh Ltd., the called-up capital is ₹8 (since the ₹2 final call was not made). The unpaid first call is ₹3, meaning ₹5 was paid. Debit Share Capital with ₹40,000, and credit Share First Call with ₹15,000 and Share Forfeiture with ₹25,000. Reissuing 2,000 shares at ₹7 as ₹8 paid requires debiting Bank with ₹14,000 and Share Forfeiture with the ₹2,000 discount, crediting Share Capital with ₹16,000. The original forfeited amount for these 2,000 shares was ₹10,000; after subtracting the ₹2,000 discount, the remaining ₹8,000 is transferred to Capital Reserve.

sub_questions.text:
रागा लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 85,000 समता अंशों को सममूल्य पर निर्गमित करने के लिए आवेदन आमन्त्रित किए। राशि का भुगतान निम्न प्रकार से देय था :
आवेदन पर - ₹ 30 प्रति अंश
आबंटन पर - ₹ 40 प्रति अंश
प्रथम तथा अन्तिम याचना पर - शेष
80,000 अंशों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए तथा सभी आवेदकों को पूर्ण रूप से अंशों का आबंटन कर दिया गया। जब आबंटन राशि देय हुई तो 300 अंशों के एक अंशधारक ने अपने अंशों पर इसका भुगतान नहीं किया तथा 500 अंशों के एक अन्य अंशधारक ने अपनी संपूर्ण अंश राशि का भुगतान कर दिया। आंबटन की अदत्त राशि सहित प्रथम एवं अन्तिम याचना पूर्ण रूप से प्राप्त हो गयी ।
रागा लिमिटेड की पुस्तकों में उपरोक्त लेनदेन की आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ कीजिए । जहाँ भी आवश्यक हो 'अदत्त-याचना खाता' तथा 'पूर्वदत्त याचना खाता' खोलिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Raga Ltd. invited applications for issuing 85,000 equity shares of ₹100 each at par. The amount was payable as follows:
On Application-₹30 per share
On Allotment-₹40 per share
On First and final call - balance
Applications were received for 80,000 shares and allotment was made to all the applicants in full. When the allotment was due, one shareholder failed to pay the amount on 300 shares held by him and another shareholder holding 500 shares paid the entire amount on his shares. The first and final call was duly received, along with arrears of allotment.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of Raga Ltd. Open 'Calls in Arrears Account' and 'Calls in Advance Account' wherever necessary.

key_points: Balance call amount = ₹100 - (₹30 + ₹40) = ₹30 per share.
Application stage: Receive and transfer ₹24,00,000 (80,000 shares × ₹30).
Allotment due stage: Share Allotment A/c Dr. ₹32,00,000 (80,000 × ₹40) To Share Capital ₹32,00,000.

Allotment receipt stage: Arrears = 300 × ₹40 = ₹12,000. Advance = 500 × ₹30 = ₹15,000. Bank receipt = ₹32,00,000 - ₹12,000 + ₹15,000 = ₹32,03,000. Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹32,03,000, Calls in Arrears A/c Dr. ₹12,000 To Share Allotment ₹32,00,000, To Calls in Advance ₹15,000.
First and Final Call due stage: Share First & Final Call A/c Dr. ₹24,00,000 (80,000 × ₹30) To Share Capital ₹24,00,000.

First and Final Call receipt stage: Regular receipt = ₹24,00,000. Less Advance adjusted = ₹15,000. Add Arrears recovered = ₹12,000. Total Bank receipt = ₹23,97,000. Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹23,97,000, Calls in Advance A/c Dr. ₹15,000 To Share First & Final Call ₹24,00,000, To Calls in Arrears ₹12,000.

sub_questions.solution: The issue is undersubscribed with 80,000 shares applied for. First, record the receipt of application money by debiting Bank and crediting Share Application with ₹24,00,000 (80,000 × ₹30). Transfer this amount to Share Capital. Next, make the allotment due by debiting Share Allotment and crediting Share Capital with ₹32,00,000 (80,000 × ₹40). During the receipt of allotment, one shareholder fails to pay on 300 shares, creating an arrear of ₹12,000. Simultaneously, another shareholder pays the balance ₹30 final call on 500 shares in advance, amounting to ₹15,000. Debit Bank with ₹32,03,000 and Calls in Arrears with ₹12,000, while crediting Share Allotment for the full ₹32,00,000 and Calls in Advance for ₹15,000. Next, make the first and final call due by debiting Share First & Final Call and crediting Share Capital with ₹24,00,000. When receiving the call money, deduct the ₹15,000 already received in advance, and add the ₹12,000 past arrear that is now recovered. Thus, debit Bank with ₹23,97,000 and Calls in Advance with ₹15,000, while crediting Share First & Final Call for ₹24,00,000 and Calls in Arrears for ₹12,000.

sub_questions.text_english:
Mitali and Karan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Their Balance Sheet as on 31st March, 2025 was as follows:
On 1st April, 2025, Nitin was admitted for 1/4 share in the profits of the firm on the following terms:
(i) Nitin will bring ₹3,00,000 as Capital and ₹1,50,000 for his share of goodwill premium in cash.
(ii) Stock was sold at ₹70,000.
(iii) Machinery was found to be overvalued by ₹8,500.
(iv) All debtors were found to be good, hence provision for doubtful debts was not required.
(v) A liability of ₹3,500 included in creditors is not likely to arise.
(vi) The market value of the investments was ₹1,40,000.
(vii) The new profit sharing ratio between Mitali, Karan and Nitin will be 2:2:1.
Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions on Nitin's admission.

key_points: Capital and Goodwill Premium Brought in: Bank A/c Dr. ₹4,50,000 To Nitin's Capital A/c ₹3,00,000, To Premium for Goodwill A/c ₹1,50,000.

Calculate Sacrificing Ratio: Old (3:2) - New (2:2:1). Mitali's sacrifice = 3/5 - 2/5 = 1/5. Karan's sacrifice = 2/5 - 2/5 = Nil. Entire goodwill goes to Mitali. Entry: Premium for Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹1,50,000 To Mitali's Capital A/c ₹1,50,000.

Investment Fluctuation: Book value ₹1,50,000. Market value ₹1,40,000. Loss of ₹10,000 is met from IFF of ₹20,000. Balance ₹10,000 goes to old partners. Entry: IFF A/c Dr. ₹20,000 To Investments ₹10,000, To Mitali's Cap A/c ₹6,000, To Karan's Cap A/c ₹4,000.
Revaluation Debits: Machinery overvalued by ₹8,500. Entry: Revaluation A/c Dr. ₹8,500 To Machinery A/c ₹8,500.
Sale of Stock: Sold for ₹70,000. Book value was ₹80,000. Loss on sale is ₹10,000. Entry: Bank A/c Dr. ₹70,000, Revaluation A/c Dr. ₹10,000 To Stock A/c ₹80,000.

Revaluation Credits: Provision for doubtful debts not required (₹10,000). Creditors not likely to arise (₹3,500). Entry: Provision for Doubtful Debts A/c Dr. ₹10,000, Creditors A/c Dr. ₹3,500 To Revaluation A/c ₹13,500.
Revaluation Loss Transfer: Total Dr = ₹18,500. Total Cr = ₹13,500. Net Loss = ₹5,000. Distributed in 3:2. Entry: Mitali's Cap A/c Dr. ₹3,000, Karan's Cap A/c Dr. ₹2,000 To Revaluation A/c ₹5,000.

sub_questions.solution: First, record Nitin's capital and goodwill injection by debiting the Bank Account for ₹4,50,000 and crediting Nitin's Capital Account for ₹3,00,000 and Premium for Goodwill for ₹1,50,000. Calculate the sacrificing ratio: Mitali sacrifices 1/5th while Karan sacrifices nothing. Consequently, the entire goodwill premium is transferred to Mitali by debiting Premium for Goodwill and crediting Mitali's Capital Account with ₹1,50,000. The investments declined in value by ₹10,000, which is covered by the Investment Fluctuation Fund (IFF) of ₹20,000. The remaining ₹10,000 of IFF is distributed in the old 3:2 ratio, crediting Mitali with ₹6,000 and Karan with ₹4,000. For revaluation losses, debit the Revaluation Account for ₹8,500 to correct the overvalued machinery. The stock sale fetches ₹70,000 (debit Bank), generating a ₹10,000 loss (debit Revaluation), which writes off the ₹80,000 Stock asset completely. For revaluation gains, reverse the unnecessary provision for doubtful debts (₹10,000) and the waived creditors (₹3,500) by debiting them and crediting the Revaluation Account for ₹13,500. Finally, clear the net revaluation loss of ₹5,000 (₹18,500 debit minus ₹13,500 credit) by debiting Mitali's Capital with ₹3,000 and Karan's Capital with ₹2,000, while crediting the Revaluation Account.

(i) संयन्त्र तथा मशीनरी का मूल्य ₹ 20,000 कम पाया गया ।
(ii) फर्नीचर का पुनर्मूल्यांकन ₹ 1,62,000 किया गया।
(iii) देनदारों पर संदिग्ध ऋणों के लिए 5% की दर से प्रावधान करना था।
(iv) फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 4,00,000 किया गया तथा इसका समायोजन शेष साझेदारों के पूँजी खातों के माध्यम से किया जायेगा ।

पुनर्मूल्यांकन खाता तथा साझेदारों के पूँजी खाते तैयार कीजिए ।
sub_questions.text_english:
Raghav, Meeta and Pranav were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. Their balance sheet as at 31st March, 2025 was as follows:
On 1st April, 2025, Pranav retired from the firm on the following terms:
(i) Plant and Machinery was found to be undervalued by ₹20,000.
(ii) Furniture was revalued at ₹1,62,000.
(iii) The provision for doubtful debts on debtors was to be created @ 5%.
(iv) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹4,00,000 and the same was to be adjusted through the capital accounts of the remaining partners.
(v) Pranav was paid in cash brought in by Raghav and Meeta in such a way so as to make the capital proportionate to the new profit sharing ratio.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Revaluation A/c: Credit Plant & Machinery ₹20,000 (undervalued). Credit Furniture ₹2,000 (1,62,000 - 1,60,000). Debit Provision for doubtful debts ₹2,000 (5% of 80,000 is 4,000, existing is 2,000, so 2,000 increase). Net Revaluation Profit = ₹20,000. Share in 5:3:2 -> Raghav ₹10,000, Meeta ₹6,000, Pranav ₹4,000.
General Reserve: Distribute ₹40,000 in 5:3:2 -> Raghav ₹20,000, Meeta ₹12,000, Pranav ₹8,000.
Goodwill adjustment: Total GW ₹4,00,000. Pranav's share = 2/10 = ₹80,000. Gaining ratio of Raghav & Meeta is 5:3. Raghav bears ₹50,000, Meeta bears ₹30,000.
Pranav's final settlement: Opening Cap ₹1,50,000 + Rev Profit ₹4,000 + Gen Res ₹8,000 + Goodwill ₹80,000 = ₹2,42,000. This is paid in cash.

Total Capital of new firm calculation: Existing adjusted caps -> Raghav (2,50,000 + 10,000 + 20,000 - 50,000) = ₹2,30,000. Meeta (2,00,000 + 6,00,000 + 12,000 - 30,000) = ₹1,88,000. Cash required to pay Pranav = ₹2,42,000. Existing cash is ₹32,000, but they bring enough to pay him off while leaving base cash unaltered (assumption: they bring exactly 2,42,000). Total Capital = 2,30,000 + 1,88,000 + 2,42,000 = ₹6,60,000.

sub_questions.solution: In the Revaluation Account, credit Plant and Machinery for ₹20,000 (since it was undervalued) and credit Furniture for the ₹2,000 increase. On the debit side, increase the Provision for Doubtful Debts by ₹2,000 (5% of 80k is 4k, minus the 2k already existing). The net revaluation profit of ₹20,000 is transferred to the partners' capital accounts in the 5:3:2 ratio: Raghav ₹10,000, Meeta ₹6,000, and Pranav ₹4,000. In the Partners' Capital Accounts, post the opening balances. Distribute the General Reserve of ₹40,000 in the old ratio, crediting Raghav ₹20,000, Meeta ₹12,000, and Pranav ₹8,000. For goodwill, Pranav's share is ₹80,000, which is debited to Raghav (₹50,000) and Meeta (₹30,000) in their 5:3 gaining ratio. Pranav's total adjusted capital balance becomes ₹2,42,000, which is paid off in cash. To determine the new capitals, calculate the combined adjusted capital of Raghav (₹2,30,000) and Meeta (₹1,88,000), and add the required cash outflow for Pranav (₹2,42,000), setting the total capital of the new firm at ₹6,60,000. Dividing this in the new 5:3 ratio yields a required closing capital of ₹4,12,500 for Raghav and ₹2,47,500 for Meeta. Consequently, Raghav brings in ₹1,82,500 in cash, and Meeta brings in ₹59,500, balancing the capital accounts.

sub_questions.text_english:
Classify the following items under the main heads and sub-heads (if any) of the Company's Balance Sheet according to schedule III, part I of Companies Act, 2013:
(i) Outstanding expenses
(ii) Work-in-progress
(iii) Capital Advances

key_points: (i) Outstanding expenses: Major Head - Current Liabilities; Sub-head - Other Current Liabilities.
(ii) Work-in-progress: Major Head - Current Assets; Sub-head - Inventories.
(iii) Capital Advances: Major Head - Non-Current Assets; Sub-head - Long-term Loans and Advances (or Other Non-Current Assets).

sub_questions.solution: According to Schedule III, Part I of the Companies Act 2013, the items are classified as follows: (i) 'Outstanding expenses' are short-term obligations, classified under the major head 'Current Liabilities' with the sub-head 'Other Current Liabilities'. (ii) 'Work-in-progress' represents partially completed inventory, classified under the major head 'Current Assets' with the sub-head 'Inventories'. (iii) 'Capital Advances' are payments made for acquiring fixed assets, classified under the major head 'Non-Current Assets' with the sub-head 'Long-term Loans and Advances'.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by cell reference, absolute cell reference and relative cell reference?

key_points: Cell Reference: The distinct alphanumeric identifier used to locate a specific cell on a spreadsheet, comprising the column letter and row number (e.g., A1).
Absolute Cell Reference: A locked reference that remains completely unchanged when a formula is copied to another location, denoted by dollar signs before the column and row (e.g., $A$1).
Relative Cell Reference: A dynamic reference that automatically adjusts and updates itself based on its new relative position when a formula is copied across rows or columns (e.g., A1).

sub_questions.solution: In spreadsheet applications like Excel, a 'Cell Reference' acts as the specific address of a cell, combining the column letter and row number (like A1) to fetch its data for formulas. An 'Absolute Cell Reference' is a strictly fixed address; by anchoring the column and row with a dollar sign (like $A$1), the reference remains entirely unchanged no matter where the formula is copied. In contrast, a 'Relative Cell Reference' (like A1) is dynamic. When a formula containing a relative reference is copied to another cell, the reference automatically shifts and adjusts relative to the direction and distance it was moved.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any three features of Computerized Accounting System.

key_points: Speed and Efficiency: Automation dramatically accelerates data entry, transaction processing, and complex calculations compared to manual methods.
High Accuracy: Eliminates the risk of human mathematical errors by automatically deriving totals and balancing ledgers based on inputted data.
Real-time Reporting: Automatically and instantaneously updates all related ledgers and generates comprehensive financial reports (like Balance Sheets) immediately after a transaction is saved.

sub_questions.solution: A Computerized Accounting System is defined by several core features that streamline financial management. First, it offers unparalleled Speed and Efficiency, as the software autonomously executes complex arithmetic and data transfers almost instantaneously. Second, it guarantees High Accuracy by completely eliminating human computational errors, provided the initial data entry is correct. Third, it enables Real-time Reporting; the moment a user inputs a single transaction, the system automatically updates all interconnected journals, ledgers, and final financial statements, allowing managers to view up-to-the-minute business data at any time.

sub_questions.text_english: The following information has been obtained from the books of Naval Ltd. Trade receivables turnover ratio of the company is 4 times, cost of revenue from operations ₹6,40,000; gross profit ratio 20%, closing trade receivables were ₹20,000 more than that in the beginning, cash revenue from operations being 33.33% of credit revenue from operations. Calculate its opening and closing trade receivables.

key_points: Gross Profit is 20% on Revenue from Operations (Sales). So, COGS is 80% of Sales. Total Sales = ₹6,40,000 / 80% = ₹8,00,000.
Cash Sales = 33.33% (1/3) of Credit Sales. Total Sales = Cash Sales + Credit Sales = (1/3) Credit Sales + Credit Sales = (4/3) Credit Sales.
Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio = Credit Sales / Average Trade Receivables = 4. Therefore, Average TR = ₹6,00,000 / 4 = ₹1,50,000.
Let Opening TR be x. Closing TR = x + 20,000. Average TR = (x + x + 20,000) / 2 = 1,50,000.

sub_questions.solution: Since the Gross Profit ratio is 20% on total sales, the Cost of Revenue from Operations represents the remaining 80%. Therefore, Total Sales equals the cost (₹6,40,000) divided by 80%, giving ₹8,00,000. We are told Cash Sales equal 33.33% (or 1/3) of Credit Sales. Since Total Sales = Cash Sales + Credit Sales, we can write Total Sales = 4/3 of Credit Sales. Solving for Credit Sales: ₹8,00,000 × 3/4 = ₹6,00,000. The Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio formula dictates that Average Trade Receivables = Credit Sales / 4. Thus, Average TR = ₹6,00,000 / 4 = ₹1,50,000. We know Closing TR is ₹20,000 more than Opening TR. Let Opening TR be x. The average formula gives (x + x + 20,000) / 2 = 1,50,000. Solving this equation yields 2x + 20,000 = 3,00,000, meaning 2x = 2,80,000, so Opening TR is ₹1,40,000. Finally, adding the ₹20,000 difference yields a Closing TR of ₹1,60,000.

sub_questions.text_english: What is Text Manipulation Function? Explain its syntax.

key_points: Text Manipulation Functions are specialized spreadsheet formulas designed to modify, parse, extract, or format text strings dynamically within cells.
Common examples include LEFT(), RIGHT(), MID(), CONCATENATE(), LEN(), and UPPER().

Syntax Explanation: A function's syntax dictates the exact structure required to execute it. It typically starts with an equals sign (=), followed by the function name, and arguments enclosed in parentheses.
Example Syntax: =LEFT(text, [num_chars]). 'text' is the cell containing the string, and 'num_chars' dictates how many characters to extract from the far left side.

sub_questions.solution: A Text Manipulation Function is an inherent spreadsheet tool specifically engineered to dynamically alter, combine, or extract data from strings of text across different cells without needing manual retyping. These functions are crucial for cleaning up formatting and organizing raw alphanumeric data. The 'syntax' refers to the strict grammatical layout that the software requires to recognize and compute the command. The universal syntax architecture requires an equals sign, the function name, and specific arguments wrapped in parentheses. For instance, the syntax for the LEFT function is `=LEFT(text, [num_chars])`. Here, 'text' represents the reference cell containing the original string, while the optional '[num_chars]' argument instructs the program on the exact number of characters to extract from the leftmost edge of that string.

key_points: Step 1: Left-click directly on the specific chart element (such as an axis, data series, or legend) within the chart area to select it.

sub_questions.solution: To effectively change the format of a selected chart element in a spreadsheet application, follow these methodical steps. First, single-click directly on the specific element you intend to modify, such as a data bar, the legend, or an axis, which will highlight it with selection handles. Second, right-click on that highlighted element to prompt a contextual drop-down menu to appear. Third, scroll down and select the 'Format [Element Name]...' command (for example, 'Format Axis' or 'Format Data Series'). This action will launch a dedicated formatting task pane, typically docked on the right side of the workspace. Finally, utilize the various tabs within this task pane to visually adjust properties such as the fill color, gradient, border width, 3D effects, and text alignment according to your precise design requirements.
